# Introduction

This page is the second phase of the wood provision update. The first phase
([physical accounts](../wood-provision/)) produced the net annual increment (NAI) of forest
available for wood supply (FAWS) by country and year, and mapped it. This page gives that flow a
monetary value, expresses it in constant prices and maps it.

The method is the one of INCA Part III [@lanotte2021] as implemented in the INCA plugin, so that
results are comparable with it. It needs three Eurostat inputs and one deflator.

1. **Value of standing timber.** `for_sup_cp` reports the output of forest trees (`P1_TR`) in
   million euro [@eurostat2026forsupcp]. Dividing it by NAI gives a unit value in euro per cubic metre.
   It is reported by few countries in the early years.
2. **Unit value of roundwood exports.** `for_basic` reports export value and volume of roundwood
   [@eurostat2026forbasic]. It is reported by almost every country and year.
3. **Ratio between the two.** Where both unit values exist, their ratio links the well-covered
   export price to the sparse timber price. The ratio is completed with averages and applied
   backwards: unit value of NAI = export unit value / ratio.
4. **Deflator.** The EU27 Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) converts nominal values to
   constant prices [@eurostat2026hicp].

The physical flow is not recomputed here. The page reads the tables that the first phase
exported to `data/outputs/results/`, so both documents stay consistent.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning in this document |
|----|----|
| Monetary value of the service | The value of the wood that the forest grows in a year, which is the net annual increment (NAI) times a price per cubic metre. |
| Unit value | A value divided by a volume, here euro per cubic metre. |
| Standing timber | Trees as they stand in the forest, before harvest. Its value is what the wood is worth before the costs of felling and transport. |
| Output of forest trees (`P1_TR`) | The item of the Eurostat forestry accounts that records the value of standing timber produced in a year. |
| Roundwood | Felled and cut timber, not yet processed. Its export price includes harvesting and transport, so it is higher than the value of standing timber. |
| Current prices | Values in the money of the year in which they occurred. Inflation makes them hard to compare across years. |
| Constant prices | Values converted to the prices of one base year, so that changes over time reflect quantities and not inflation. |
| Deflator | The factor that converts a current value to constant prices. It is the price index of the base year divided by the index of the year of the value. |
| HICP | The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices of Eurostat, used here as the general price index. |

## Why the method uses two prices

The value of standing timber is the ideal price for the service, but countries rarely report it,
mainly before 2012. Roundwood export prices are reported by almost every country and year, but they
include the costs of harvesting and transport, so they are not the same thing. The method uses
the countries and years where both prices exist to measure how far apart the two are (the
ratio). It then turns the well-covered export price into an estimate of the timber price by dividing
by that ratio. In the years and countries with no timber price, the ratio is replaced by an
average, which is the weakest part of the method and is reported openly in the tables below.

::: {.callout-important}
## Run the physical document first

This page reads `data/outputs/results/wood_nai_faws_country_year.rds` and the 1 km FAWS shares
in `data/inputs/faws/`. Both are committed to the repository, so nothing needs to be rerun unless
the physical series changes.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Constant prices use a single base year

The base year is `base_year` in the parameters chunk. It is set to 2010, the base year of the fish provision
accounts, so that the services share one price level and can be added or compared (the INCA plugin
uses 2000). The choice of base year changes the level of the constant-price series but not its shape. Changing it does not touch the nominal
values, because the deflator is applied in one step at the end.
:::

# Preliminaries

## Packages and helper functions

```{r}
#| label: libraries

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(flextable)

source("scripts/helpers_wood.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
source("scripts/helpers_monetary.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
```

## Parameters

A country with some observations is completed with its own average, because its price level is
the best guide to its missing years. A country with no observations at all is completed with the
EU average, taken over recent years, where coverage is better. The averages that complete the gaps
use the same windows as the INCA plugin: the country mean over the whole series, and the EU mean over
the more recent years. The
plugin stops at 2021 because of the data it had; the window here runs to 2023, the last year
with broad coverage.

```{r}
#| label: parameters

years_all <- 2000:2024
years_report <- c(2000, 2006, 2012, 2018, 2024)
base_year <- 2010

# Windows for the averages that fill gaps
country_years <- 2000:2023
eu_years <- 2012:2023

# Inputs
nai_file <- "data/outputs/results/wood_nai_faws_country_year.rds"
sup_file <- "data/inputs/eurostat/for_sup_cp_p1tr.rds"
basic_file <- "data/inputs/eurostat/for_basic_rw_exports.rds"
hicp_file <- "data/inputs/eurostat/hicp_eu27.rds"
countries_file <- "data/inputs/gis/NUTS_RG_01M_2024_3035_LEVL0.gpkg"
faws_share_file <- "data/inputs/faws/FAWS_2020_EU27_1km.tif"

# Outputs
results_dir <- "data/outputs/results"
gis_dir <- "data/outputs/gis"
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(gis_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Preparing the Eurostat inputs

The script `scripts/04_download_eurostat_monetary.R` downloads the three Eurostat extracts and
saves compact files in `data/inputs/eurostat/`. It is run once and needs internet access.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-inputs
#| eval: false

source("scripts/04_download_eurostat_monetary.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
```

# Loading the inputs

All series are placed on a complete grid of the 27 member states and the years 2000 to 2024, so
that every missing value is visible as a missing cell.

```{r}
#| label: load-inputs

countries <- st_read(countries_file, quiet = TRUE)
eu27 <- countries$geo[countries$eu27]

nai <- readRDS(nai_file) |>
  on_grid(eu27, years_all, "nai_faws_1000m3")

timber_value <- readRDS(sup_file) |>
  on_grid(eu27, years_all, "value_mio_eur")

exports <- readRDS(basic_file)

hicp <- readRDS(hicp_file)
```

## How much was reported

```{r}
#| label: availability

tibble(
  Year = years_report,
  `Timber value (for_sup_cp)` = sapply(years_report, \(y) sum(!is.na(timber_value$value[timber_value$year == y]))),
  `Export value and volume (for_basic)` = sapply(years_report, \(y) {
    sum(!is.na(exports$exports_ths_eur[exports$year == y] / exports$exports_ths_m3[exports$year == y]))
  })
) |>
  show_table(digits = 0)
```

The table counts member states out of 27. Timber value is reported by only a few countries in 2000
and 2006, and by almost all of them from 2012 on, so the method has to lean on the export price
in the early years.

# Unit values

## Unit value of NAI

The timber value is divided by NAI, and the unit is converted from million euro per thousand cubic
metres to euro per cubic metre. A country-year without NAI gets no unit value.

```{r}
#| label: unit-value-nai

unit_value_nai <- nai |>
  rename(nai = value) |>
  left_join(timber_value |> rename(timber = value), by = c("geo", "year")) |>
  mutate(value = if_else(nai > 0, 1000 * timber / nai, NA_real_)) |>
  select(geo, year, value)
```

## Unit value of roundwood exports

Export value (thousand euro) divided by export volume (thousand cubic metres) gives euro per cubic
metre. Gaps are filled with the country mean, or with the EU mean when a country never reports.

```{r}
#| label: unit-value-exports

unit_value_exports <- exports |>
  mutate(value = if_else(exports_ths_m3 > 0, exports_ths_eur / exports_ths_m3, NA_real_)) |>
  on_grid(eu27, years_all, "value")

unit_value_exports_filled <- fill_with_means(unit_value_exports, country_years, eu_years)
```

## Ratio of export price to timber price

The ratio is the export unit value divided by the timber unit value. A ratio of 3 means that
roundwood sells for three times the value of the same wood standing. It is computed from the
reported values only, before any filling, because a ratio built from filled values would contain
no new information. Infinite values, which come from a zero timber value, are treated as missing.
The gaps are then filled with the same averages.

```{r}
#| label: ratio

ratio <- unit_value_exports |>
  rename(exports = value) |>
  left_join(unit_value_nai |> rename(nai_uv = value), by = c("geo", "year")) |>
  mutate(
    value = exports / nai_uv,
    value = if_else(is.finite(value), value, NA_real_)
  ) |>
  select(geo, year, value)

ratio_filled <- fill_with_means(ratio, country_years, eu_years)
```

The share of the 27 ratios that are observed in each reporting year shows how much of the result
rests on averages.

```{r}
#| label: ratio-sources

ratio_filled |>
  filter(year %in% years_report) |>
  count(year, fill) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = fill, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(Year = year) |>
  show_table(digits = 0)
```

## Completed unit value of NAI

The completed unit value divides the export unit value by the ratio. Where the ratio is observed,
this returns the observed timber unit value.

```{r}
#| label: unit-value-final

unit_value <- unit_value_exports_filled |>
  select(geo, year, export_uv = value) |>
  left_join(
    ratio_filled |> select(geo, year, ratio = value, ratio_fill = fill),
    by = c("geo", "year")
  ) |>
  mutate(unit_value_eur_m3 = export_uv / ratio)
```

The chart shows the completed unit value for every country in the reporting years. A few countries
sit far above the rest, and they are the ones whose ratio comes from the average of a small
number of observations.

```{r}
#| label: unit-value-chart
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 9

unit_value |>
  filter(year %in% years_report) |>
  mutate(geo = reorder(geo, unit_value_eur_m3, FUN = median)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = unit_value_eur_m3, y = geo, colour = ratio_fill)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~year, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Unit value of NAI (euro per m3, current prices)", y = NULL, colour = "Ratio")
```

# Monetary flow

## Nominal value

The monetary flow is NAI times the completed unit value, in million euro at current prices.

```{r}
#| label: nominal

monetary <- nai |>
  rename(nai_1000m3 = value) |>
  left_join(unit_value, by = c("geo", "year")) |>
  mutate(value_mio_eur_current = nai_1000m3 * unit_value_eur_m3 / 1000)
```

## Constant prices

Prices rose between 2000 and 2024, so a euro in 2024 buys less than a euro in 2010. To compare
years, the HICP index is rebased so that the base year equals 1, and each nominal value is
multiplied by the deflator of its year. Deflators are above 1 before the base year, where prices were
lower, and below 1 after it. The result is in million euro of the base year. The same index is used
for all countries, because the question is how the general price level moved and not how timber
prices moved.

```{r}
#| label: constant-prices

deflator <- make_deflator(hicp, "hicp_2015", base_year)

monetary <- monetary |>
  left_join(deflator, by = "year") |>
  mutate(value_mio_eur_constant = value_mio_eur_current * deflator)
```

```{r}
#| label: deflator-table

deflator |>
  filter(year %in% years_report) |>
  rename(Year = year, `Deflator (base year = 1)` = deflator) |>
  show_table(digits = 3)
```

## EU totals

The table sums the 27 countries in the reporting years. For comparison, INCA Part III reports an EU
total of 23,745 million euro for 2000 [@lanotte2021]. That figure uses a different country set
and vintage of the data, so the comparison is a check of order of magnitude.

```{r}
#| label: eu-totals

monetary |>
  filter(year %in% years_report) |>
  summarise(
    `NAI (million m3)` = sum(nai_1000m3) / 1000,
    `Current prices (million euro)` = sum(value_mio_eur_current),
    `Constant prices (million euro)` = sum(value_mio_eur_constant),
    .by = year
  ) |>
  rename(Year = year) |>
  show_table(digits = 0)
```

# Spatial component

The monetary flow is spread with the spatial key of the physical document: inside each country,
in proportion to the share of every 1 km cell that is FAWS. Every cell of a country therefore has
the same unit value, and the pattern of the monetary map is the pattern of the NAI map.

```{r}
#| label: spatial-inputs

faws_share <- rast(faws_share_file)
eu_countries <- vect(countries_file)
eu_countries <- eu_countries[eu_countries$eu27, ]

country_ids <- make_country_ids(eu_countries, faws_share)
weight_sums <- country_weight_sums(faws_share, country_ids)
```

To keep the repository light, the maps are written in constant prices only. They are
the ones used to compare years. The nominal values by country are in the exported tables.

```{r}
#| label: spread-value

for (yr in years_report) {
  value_map <- spread_totals(
    totals = monetary |> filter(year == yr) |> select(geo, value = value_mio_eur_constant),
    weight = faws_share,
    country_ids = country_ids,
    weight_sums = weight_sums
  )
  names(value_map) <- paste0("value_constant_", yr)
  writeRaster(
    value_map,
    file.path(gis_dir, sprintf("wood_value_constant_1km_%s.tif", yr)),
    overwrite = TRUE,
    datatype = "FLT4S",
    gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "PREDICTOR=3", "TILED=YES")
  )
}
```

## Conservation check

```{r}
#| label: conservation-check

value_maps <- rast(file.path(gis_dir, sprintf("wood_value_constant_1km_%s.tif", years_report)))

national_totals <- monetary |>
  filter(year %in% years_report) |>
  summarise(total = sum(value_mio_eur_constant), .by = year) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  pull(total)

tibble(
  Year = years_report,
  `Sum of maps (million euro)` = global(value_maps, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]],
  `Sum of national values (million euro)` = national_totals
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (`Sum of maps (million euro)` / `Sum of national values (million euro)` - 1)) |>
  show_table(digits = 2)
```

## Maps

The maps are shown at 10 km, as the sum of 100 cells of 1 km.

```{r}
#| label: value-maps
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10

map_data <- aggregate(value_maps, fact = 10, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE) |>
  as.data.frame(xy = TRUE) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("value_constant_"), names_to = "year", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(year = sub("value_constant_", "", year)) |>
  filter(value > 0)

ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_tile(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value)) +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = NA, linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(transform = "sqrt", name = "Million euro\n(base-year prices)\nper 10 km cell") +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(2.6e6, 6.6e6), ylim = c(1.4e6, 5.4e6), datum = NA) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

# Refinement: Corine Land Cover forest by year

::: {.callout-important}
## Optional refinement with its own outputs

The maps above are the baseline. This section repeats the spatial step with the spatial key of the
Corine refinement of the [physical document](../wood-provision/), which is the 100 m overlap of FAWS
and Corine Land Cover forest of each epoch (CLC 2018 is used for 2024). It writes only to
`data/outputs/gis/corine_refinement/` and `data/outputs/results/corine_refinement/`, and every file name
starts with `corine_refinement_`.
:::

The national monetary values are the same as in the baseline, so only their placement inside each
country changes. The weights are the 1 km files produced by `scripts/05_prepare_clc.R`.

```{r}
#| label: clc-weights

clc_epochs <- c("2000", "2006", "2012", "2018")
clc_for_year <- c(`2000` = "2000", `2006` = "2006", `2012` = "2012", `2018` = "2018", `2024` = "2018")

refine_gis_dir <- file.path(gis_dir, "corine_refinement")
refine_results_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "corine_refinement")
dir.create(refine_gis_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(refine_results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

clc_weights <- lapply(clc_epochs, \(e) rast(sprintf("data/inputs/corine/FAWS_x_CLC%s_1km.tif", e)))
names(clc_weights) <- clc_epochs

clc_weight_sums <- lapply(clc_weights, country_weight_sums, country_ids = country_ids)
```

```{r}
#| label: clc-spread-value

for (yr in years_report) {
  epoch <- clc_for_year[[as.character(yr)]]
  refined_map <- spread_totals(
    totals = monetary |> filter(year == yr) |> select(geo, value = value_mio_eur_constant),
    weight = clc_weights[[epoch]],
    country_ids = country_ids,
    weight_sums = clc_weight_sums[[epoch]]
  )
  names(refined_map) <- paste0("value_clc_", yr)
  writeRaster(
    refined_map,
    file.path(refine_gis_dir, sprintf("corine_refinement_wood_value_constant_1km_%s.tif", yr)),
    overwrite = TRUE,
    datatype = "FLT4S",
    gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "PREDICTOR=3", "TILED=YES")
  )
}
```

## Conservation check

```{r}
#| label: clc-conservation

refined_maps <- rast(
  file.path(refine_gis_dir, sprintf("corine_refinement_wood_value_constant_1km_%s.tif", years_report))
)

tibble(
  Year = years_report,
  `CLC epoch` = unname(clc_for_year[as.character(years_report)]),
  `Sum of maps (million euro)` = global(refined_maps, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]],
  `Sum of national values (million euro)` = national_totals
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (`Sum of maps (million euro)` / `Sum of national values (million euro)` - 1)) |>
  show_table(digits = 2)
```

## Comparison with the baseline

Each country has one unit value, so inside a country the monetary map is the NAI map multiplied
by a constant. The comparison below therefore shows the same pattern of differences as in the
physical document, in money terms. The table gives the share of the value that sits in a different
10 km cell, and the correlation between the two maps.

```{r}
#| label: clc-comparison

base_10km <- aggregate(value_maps, fact = 10, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)
refined_10km <- aggregate(refined_maps, fact = 10, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)

comparison <- tibble(
  Year = years_report,
  `Value moved (% of total)` = sapply(seq_along(years_report), \(i) {
    100 * 0.5 * global(abs(refined_10km[[i]] - base_10km[[i]]), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]] /
      global(base_10km[[i]], "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
  }),
  `Value moved (million euro)` = sapply(seq_along(years_report), \(i) {
    0.5 * global(abs(refined_10km[[i]] - base_10km[[i]]), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
  }),
  `Correlation of cells` = sapply(seq_along(years_report), \(i) {
    cor(values(base_10km[[i]]), values(refined_10km[[i]]), use = "complete.obs")
  })
)

show_table(comparison, digits = 2)
```

The map shows the difference in value (refined minus baseline) for 2018. Red cells gain value with the
refinement and blue cells lose it.

```{r}
#| label: clc-difference-map
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6

diff_data <- (refined_10km[[4]] - base_10km[[4]]) |>
  setNames("difference") |>
  as.data.frame(xy = TRUE) |>
  filter(abs(difference) > 0)

diff_limit <- as.numeric(quantile(abs(diff_data$difference), 0.99))

ggplot(diff_data) +
  geom_tile(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = pmax(pmin(difference, diff_limit), -diff_limit))) +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = NA, linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",
    name = "Million euro\n(2010 prices)\nper 10 km cell"
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(2.6e6, 6.6e6), ylim = c(1.4e6, 5.4e6), datum = NA) +
  theme_void()
```

The refined maps depend on a second dataset that was mapped independently of FAWS, so they are
offered as an option and the baseline remains the main result.

```{r}
#| label: clc-export

export_table(
  comparison |> rename_with(\(x) gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)),
  "corine_refinement_value_comparison_with_baseline",
  dir = refine_results_dir
)
```

# Exports

```{r}
#| label: export-tables

monetary_export <- monetary |>
  transmute(
    geo, year,
    nai_1000m3,
    export_uv_eur_m3 = export_uv,
    ratio_export_to_timber = ratio,
    ratio_source = ratio_fill,
    unit_value_eur_m3,
    value_mio_eur_current,
    deflator,
    value_mio_eur_constant
  )

export_table(monetary_export, "wood_value_country_year")

writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    value_report_years = monetary_export |> filter(year %in% years_report),
    deflator = deflator,
    parameters = tibble(
      parameter = c("base_year", "country_years", "eu_years", "deflator"),
      value = c(
        base_year,
        paste(range(country_years), collapse = "-"),
        paste(range(eu_years), collapse = "-"),
        "HICP all items, EU27 (2020), annual average"
      )
    )
  ),
  file.path(results_dir, "wood_value_summary.xlsx")
)
```

# Downloads

```{r}
#| label: downloads

downloads <- tibble(
  File = c(
    "wood_value_country_year.xlsx",
    "wood_value_country_year.rds",
    "wood_value_summary.xlsx",
    sprintf("wood_value_constant_1km_%s.tif", years_report)
  ),
  Folder = c(rep("results", 3), rep("gis", length(years_report))),
  Description = c(
    "Unit values, nominal and constant-price value by country and year, with the origin of the ratio",
    "The same panel as an R object",
    "Reporting-year table, deflator and parameters",
    sprintf("Value of NAI of FAWS in %s, million euro in 2010 prices per 1 km cell, EPSG:3035", years_report)
  )
) |>
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      File = c(
        "corine_refinement_value_comparison_with_baseline.xlsx",
        sprintf("corine_refinement_wood_value_constant_1km_%s.tif", years_report)
      ),
      Folder = c("results/corine_refinement", rep("gis/corine_refinement", length(years_report))),
      Description = c(
        "Refinement: how far the refined value maps differ from the baseline maps, by year",
        sprintf("Refinement: value of NAI of FAWS in %s spread over FAWS and CLC forest, million euro in 2010 prices per 1 km cell", years_report)
      )
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(Path = file.path("../../../data/outputs", Folder, File))

flextable(downloads, col_keys = c("File", "Description")) |>
  compose(
    j = "File",
    value = as_paragraph(hyperlink_text(x = File, url = Path))
  ) |>
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
  autofit()
```

# Limitations

- The unit value of timber is observed for few countries before 2012. In those years most of the
  value comes from the export price divided by an average ratio, so the monetary series is better
  read as an estimate than as a measurement.
- Roundwood export prices include harvesting and transport, whereas `for_sup_cp` values standing
  trees. The ratio between them is large (a median of several times), and it is the weakest link
  of the method. It is inherited from the INCA approach.
- NAI of FAWS partly comes from total forest NAI (see the physical document), and the monetary
  value inherits that. The sensitivity check of the physical document applies here proportionally.
- A single EU27 deflator is applied to all countries, as in the plugin.
- The baseline spatial key is a 2020 map, so maps of earlier years apply the 2020 pattern. The
  Corine refinement adds change over time, with the limits discussed in the physical document.
